chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Leaving Philadelphia's Madhouse for Atlantic City
summary: Asked about the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, Wooding says he first heard it in Atlantic City, to which he returned in 1920 as it was like Las Vegas.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, in 1918, when you were back at the Madhouse, the first jazz recordings have come out by then. By the Original Dixieland Jazz Band. This white group from New Orleans, do you remember?
I didn't hear that until I went to Atlantic City.
You see, I didn't stay there no longer than -- you know, when it got to be May, Atlantic City was a great place in those days. What Las Vegas is today.

What they're trying to do at Ocean City, Maryland. And, Atlantic City -- and, we had so much fun in Atlantic City. And there was always newcomers there. It was -- so, right away I chucked Jake's place. I told Jake I was very thankful for having the job. But, now it was time for me to go to Atlantic City. I didn't have anything to go to. But you never needed anything to go to in Atlantic City.
So, was that the summer of 1918, that
you went back to Atlantic City?
No, this was the ending of '19, because I came back in '19 from --
Oh, right. Right. So it was really at the end of the season, when you came back.
Uh hunh. No, that was twenty when I went back to Atlantic City.
